html:
The Nepal earthquake, also called the Gorkha earthquake, struck central Nepal just before noon on 25 April 2015. It measured about 7.8 and killed nearly 9,000 people, most in Nepal, with more in India, China and Bangladesh.

The centre was in Gorkha district, about 85 km northwest of Kathmandu. In the Kathmandu valley, old brick houses and many temples of the three royal cities fell, including much of the Durbar Squares and the Dharahara tower. In the mountains, villages were cut off by landslides, and an avalanche at the base camp of Mount Everest killed climbers and guides. A second large quake on 12 May added to the damage.

The Himalaya are still rising as India pushes north into Asia, and great quakes like this one and the 1934 Bihar and Nepal earthquake are part of that. Rebuilding was slow. Some temples were restored over the following decade, and the long delayed Constitution of Nepal was passed that September.
